newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Stadium group to raise A$364.4 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Stadium group to raise A$364.4 mln.

text.p: The Australia Stadium Consortium, which will build the main stadium for the Sydney 2000 Olympics, said on Tuesday it would raise A$364.4 million through the sale of passes to attend Sydney 2000 Games events.
Australia Stadium said the estimated cost to build the stadium would be A$615 million.
It said it would issue 34,400 gold packages at A$10,000 each and would seek to raise a further A$20 million from the private placement of 600 platinium packages.

Australia Stadium said the gold package would give investors a guaranteed seat at each stadium session during the 2000 Games, the ability to arrange up to six seats next to each other, stadium club membership for over 30 years from 1999, entry to most post-Olympic sporting events at no extra cost.

It said the gold package would also give access to a gold members reserve area and 1,000 units in a trust stapled to 1,000 shares in Staduim Australia Management, which is to be listed on the Australian Stock Exchange.
The Australia Stadium consortium is headed by investment bankers Hambros Australia, a unit of Hambros Bank and Australian construction group Mutliplex Construction.
The consortium won the right to build the 110,000 seater Olympic Stadium, which will be the centrepiece of the 2000 Games, in January.
Constrution of the Olympic Stadium at Homebush in Sydney's west, is expected to be finished in 1999, with the Australia Stadium operating the stadium for a 30 year period.
